subject: Re: Follow-up: Reranker integration & eval plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Reranker integration & eval plan

Thanks again for the time today, Daniel — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

TL:DR: Acme is planning a reranking layer on product search results. You want to validate whether Redwood's reranker + embeddings pipeline improves relevance metrics vs your current BM25 baseline and estimate integration effort.

Recap from call:
- Goal: improve product search relevance (Homepage search + category pages) and reduce zero-result noise.
- Primary success metrics: NDCG@10 uplift, Recall@5, and business lift measured by click-through rate on top 3 results.
- Data available: anonymized query logs, relevance labels for ~5k queries, product metadata + embeddings currently generated offline.
- Constraints: must run in Acme's VPC for PII-sensitive SKU tags (you flagged GDPR concerns).

Proposed next steps (action items):
1) Technical discovery with our SE (Dev Patel) to confirm auth/routing and SDK setup for Acme Private deployment (target early July).
2) Share a small eval pack (we requested a sample of labeled queries) — Marissa to provide Redwood sample template and expected format.
3) Redwood will run a baseline offline eval (NDCG/Recall/MRR) and propose top_k recommendations (top_k for candidate pool and reranker cutoff).
4) If offline looks good, plan a canary integration (server-side rerank endpoint in front of search) + A/B test.

Attachments: sample CSV template attached (reranker-eval-sample.csv) — please fill with a few representative queries and labels. Also linking our architecture diagram for the proposed routing pattern (attachment: architecture-diagram-v1.png).

Open questions we flagged for Dev on the technical call (to be answered in the SE follow-up):
- Auth: do you prefer API-key & VPC peering or mTLS + private endpoint?
- Routing: will you call Redwood's reranker as a post-processing step from your search service, or do you want us to embed a sidecar that receives candidate lists?
- Indexing/candidates: how are you generating candidate pools today (BM25 top 100?) — this impacts top_k recommendation.

Proposed timings: SE discovery next Tue/Wed (6/29-6/30). Let me know availability.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@acmeretail.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Reranker integration & eval plan

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect, and yes, the timeline works. A few quick clarifications:

- We'll try to get you ~5k labeled queries by EOD Monday; those are sampled from last quarter's queries with human relevance labels (0/1/2).
- For deployment we prefer VPC peering + private endpoint if possible (our security team is cautious about mTLS complexity right now). We'll confirm after the SE call.
- Candidate pool today is BM25 top 100, then we apply simple business rules before returning top 10. We're interested in both replacing the final sort and augmenting candidate scoring.

Question: for offline eval, should we provide textual product descriptions + metadata fields? We can include title, description, category, price_bucket, and stock status.

We'll plan to be available for the SE discovery on 6/29 morning PST (9–11am). Priya will coordinate the calendar invite.

—Daniel
Daniel Kim
Sr. Product Manager, Search
Acme Retail

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@acmeretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 18:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Reranker integration & eval plan — technical questions

Hey Daniel — quick technical notes ahead of our discovery call so we can prep an architecture sketch: 

1) SDK / Auth options:
   - Option A (recommended for Private): VPC peering + private API endpoint. Auth via API key stored in your KMS; we support per-client keys and rotation.
   - Option B: mTLS + mutual certs if you need two-way cert verification. Slightly more setup on your infra side.

2) Routing patterns we commonly implement:
   - Post-process rerank: your search service requests BM25 top 100 -> call Redwood.rerank(candidates, query) -> Redwood returns reranked IDs + scores. Minimal change in your stack.
   - Sidecar pattern: lightweight service next to search that calls Redwood and injects scores before final scoring. Useful if you want local caching and lower latency.

3) API details (reranking endpoint):
   - Endpoint: POST /v1/rerank
   - Payload: {"query": "string", "candidates": [ {"id": "string", "text": "string", "metadata": {...} } ] }
   - Response: list of {id, score, explanation} — we can include structured tool-calling-style outputs if you want downstream systems to act on entities.

4) Top_k tuning guidance:
   - Candidate pool: keep to top 100 from BM25 for initial experiments.
   - Reranker top_k: typically we score all candidates but recommend truncating final output to top 10 for client-side UX. For evaluation, compute metrics at k=1,3,5,10.

5) Metrics & evaluation design:
   - Offline: NDCG@5/10, MRR, Recall@k. Use bootstrap CI if sample is small.
   - Online: CTR on top-3, conversion uplift, and query success rate.

6) Sample sizes: with 5k labeled queries we should get stable NDCG estimates for initial signal; 20–50k better for small uplifts.

7) Data format: please include product textual fields (title, description), product_id, and label (0/1/2). CSV template attached. If you need a mapper for your internal fields to our candidate schema, we can provide a small script.

I'll bring a short architecture sketch to the call outlining VPC peering + private endpoint and two routing patterns. If you can share any latency SLOs for search (p99 target), that helps us recommend batching/cache settings.

Thanks — Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Reranker integration & eval plan — next steps & calendar

Thanks everyone — confirming next steps and owners: 

- Daniel / Priya: share the labeled sample CSV by Monday EOD (ACME) — include product text fields and labels as discussed. (Attachment template: reranker-eval-sample.csv)
- Dev (SE): will run offline eval on the sample and return a short report (NDCG@5/10, MRR, Recall@k) + recommended top_k and candidate pool size by 7/2.
- Marissa: will prepare a canary/POC pricing estimate and draft NDA addendum for Private deployment.
- Lauren: will coordinate pilot SOW and HubSpot deal record (DEAL-2391).

Calendar: I've tentatively booked a 60-min SE discovery on Tue 6/29 at 9:30am PDT — invite sent to Daniel/Priya/Dev. If that doesn't work, let me know and we'll adjust.

Deliverables we expect after SE discovery:
- Architecture diagram (private endpoint + routing pattern) — Redwood to provide (see attached draft).
- Offline eval report + top_k recommendations.
- Pilot SOW + pricing range for a 3-month POC.

If there's anything I missed, call it out. Looking forward to the discovery.

Best — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
